investigation.title: Remote Agent Swarm Gateway 502 — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared ELB Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-15T12:35–12:36Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when the eval runner issued POST /api/agents. Because the failure occurred before any agent was created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS Elastic Load Balancer in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", causing POST /api/agents to fail immediately for every remote-agent check. Because the failure is at the network/infrastructure boundary (ELB → swarm backend), no agent identity or VM state was ever established, which is why all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing. The root cause is uncertain between: (a) the ELB target group having no healthy targets, (b) a transient network partition between the production-api and the swarm ELB, or (c) the swarm service itself being down or misconfigured behind the ELB. No suspect code changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to implicate a recent deployment.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS Elastic Load Balancer in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The root cause is uncertain between: (a) the ELB target group having no healthy targets, (b) a transient network partition between the production-api and the swarm ELB, or (c) the swarm service itself being down or misconfigured behind the ELB.
